Sliding-window attention at 5T

A deep comparison of GPT-OSS-like and Inkling-like local/global attention, the design space between them, and hybrids using MLA, DSA sparse retrieval, KDA linear state, or DeepSeek-V4 compressed global layers.

Executive result

SWA’s benefit depends on what “global” means

Plain GQA-based SWA reduces cache in proportion to the global-layer frequency, but full GQA KV is still wide. Replacing the occasional global layer with a sparse, recurrent, or compressed representation changes the capacity picture far more than shrinking a 512-token local window.

Native reference patterns

Two very different uses of local attention

Tinker is the customization platform; Inkling is Thinking Machines’ model. The controlled 5T rows preserve each attention pattern and head geometry where practical, while normalizing the MoE body, depth, and total scale.

AIC’s SOL path treats routed assignments as evenly balanced and maximally non-overlapping until the local expert pool is exhausted. At DEP64, c/r=1 means 64 simultaneous requests globally—not one request globally—so the model already saturates all 19 experts resident on every rank. This is an aggregate idealization, not a token-level routing or busiest-rank simulation.

Hybrid global paths

Five ways to supply long-range information

Holding the local stack at 5:1 and W512 exposes the real trade: dense GQA, latent attention, sparse retrieval, recurrent linear state, or V4-style compression. DSA wins fixed-c/r latency here; V4 wins cache density.

5:1 architectureGlobal memory behaviorKV GiB/requestGB c/r=4GB 50-TPS c/rRubin 50-TPS c/rMemory max c/rMemory max globalRubin TPS at memory max
Memory-max global concurrency is memory-max c/r × DEP64. It is a residency limit, not a claim that every resident request meets a useful latency target. GB300 and projected Rubin use the same 277.55 GiB/rank capacity assumption here, so their admission limits are identical.
DSA keeps full-context retrieval metadata and latent KV for only the periodic global layers but reads top-2048 entries during decode. KDA keeps a constant-size recurrent state. V4’s compressed hierarchy has the smallest resident representation but the highest architectural novelty.

Latency–memory frontier

The hybrid global representation is decisive

The scatter plot compares every controlled profile at GB300 c/r=4. Moving upward is faster; moving left uses less KV. Window/ratio variations form families, while mechanism changes create the large jumps.

Service-level boundaries

Can Rubin fill the available cache?

For plain GQA SWA, yes: the cache is wide enough that Rubin reaches physical capacity while retaining more than 50 SOL TPS/user. Periodic DSA preserves this useful-residency property at much higher concurrency. Ultra-compact recurrent and V4 hybrids do not: capacity expands much faster than their throughput ceiling.

GPT-OSS-like 1:1

At physical c/r=30: GB300 ≈25.0 TPS/user; Rubin ≈66.5.

Inkling-like 5:1

At physical c/r=44: GB300 ≈23.9 TPS/user; Rubin ≈62.7.

5:1 SWA/DSA top-2048

At physical c/r=116: GB300 ≈43.4 TPS/user; Rubin ≈75.7. Rubin can use every resident slot above 50 SOL TPS.

5:1 SWA/KDA

At physical c/r=632: GB300 ≈8.2 TPS/user; Rubin ≈13.7. The constant state makes admission far larger than useful concurrency.

5:1 SWA/V4 compressed

At physical c/r=994: GB300 ≈5.6 TPS/user; Rubin ≈9.0. Filling memory is no longer sensible.

100% V4 compressed control

The SWA/V4 hybrid raises the 50-TPS boundary from 78→99 c/r on GB300 and 159→179 on Rubin.

Interpretation

What the sweep teaches us

The most robust findings are architectural relationships, not the exact raw-SOL values.

01

Ratio is the primary SWA knob

At 256K, the 512-token local window is already tiny. Reducing global layers from one-half to one-sixth cuts the dominant full-context work; tuning 512 to 128 barely matters.

02

KV width can erase sparsity gains

GPT-OSS-like head dimension 64 halves KV bytes relative to the common 128-dim control. Inkling’s extra local KV heads cost little at long context because only 512 entries survive locally.

03

Periodic DSA is the latency sweet spot

At 5:1 it leads GB300 c/r=4 at 149.8 TPS/user and Rubin can fill all 116 slots/rank at 75.7 TPS/user. The cost is a full-context index and latent KV on every DSA global layer, plus irregular top-k kernels.

04

Recurrent versus compressed globals

At 5:1, KDA needs 0.35 GiB/request and V4 needs 0.23. V4 is modestly faster here; KDA has truly context-constant state but carries greater quality risk as the global information path.

05

More cache can become unusable

Rubin can fill plain SWA and 5:1 SWA/DSA above 50 TPS/user. The compact KDA and V4 hybrids run out of throughput long before their much larger memory-admission boundaries.

06

Quality risk rises with local depth

1:1 is the conservative endpoint; 5:1 has stronger systems scaling but asks five successive local transformations to carry information between global retrieval layers.

KV bytes ≈ Σlocal min(context, window)·KVwidth + Σglobal global-state(context)

Method and limits

How rigorous is this comparison?

AIC directly prices windowed/full GQA. MLA, V4, and KDA use AIC-derived per-layer primitives; DSA uses the earlier explicit SOL formula with its shared-index cadence averaged over the global layers. All are additive composites on the identical 5T body.

AIC SOL latencyAll 22,616 no-spec reference points use SOL operation models; the source audit found zero non-SOL latency contributions.
Explicit KV accountingFP8 cache bytes are calculated per layer. SWA is window-capped; each global mechanism uses its own full, latent, recurrent, or compressed state.
Common 5T body61 layers, hidden 7168, 1216 routed experts, top-25, zero shared experts, intermediate 3072, DEP64. Attention is the controlled variable.
Ideal expert balanceAIC spreads routed assignments evenly across expert ranks and assumes unique experts until each rank’s resident pool is saturated. It does not model token-level correlations, hot experts, or stragglers.
Faithful-inspired, not clonedNative head dimensions, KV asymmetry, ratios, and windows are preserved where possible, but depth and Q-head count are normalized to the common body.
Hybrid uncertaintyThe additive DSA/KDA/V4 hybrids are counterfactuals, not implemented checkpoints. Kernel fusion, layout transitions, and information-routing quality are not measured.
Decode-onlyResident 32K/256K/1M cache with no prefill, scheduling, queueing, framework loss, imbalance, or production-efficiency discount.
Quality out of scopeSOL cannot predict whether a 3:1 or 5:1 stack preserves retrieval, training stability, or model capability.
